newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danubius hits new high on Budapest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Danubius hits new high on Budapest bourse.

text.p: Most leading issues of the Budapest Stock Exchange remained flat on Friday as hesitancy prevailed among the investors, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 3,550.20 points, up 10.74.
Traders explained the uncertainty not only by U.S. rate hike fears but by the Russian president's bad health, too.
"The market was uncertain where prices will move to," said Attila Hunyadi of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz Kft.
"There are more reasons for this uncertainty such as Yeltsin's health, employee shares of Richter and MOL and energy price increase," he said.
The market expects fresh supply of pharmaceuticals Richter and oil firm MOL shares to the market later this year.
"This may be an additional supply which may push prices lower on the bourse," Hunyadi said.
Richter ended at 8,385 forints, down 65, while MOL remained unchanged.
The government postponed the energy price increase to January 1, 1997 from October 1, but there has not yet been any decision on its size.
Hotelier Danubius rose to a new high of 3,035 forints on what traders attributed to local purchases.
Inter-Europa Bank gained 2,900 forints to end at 37,950.
